AddonRow.description:
One subscription add-on row, with its activation status for
the calling store. Mirrors the legacy ADDONS_CATALOG entry +
a derived `is_active` from the store's CSV addon list.
AddonRow.title: AddonRow

AdminAuditLogResponse.description:
Page-shaped response. `total` is the count after filters
are applied; `total_pages` is rounded up against the fixed
per-page constant so the SPA can render the pager without
knowing the magic number.
AdminAuditLogResponse.title: AdminAuditLogResponse

AdminAuditRow.description:
One row in the merged operator audit-log feed.

`source` is "operator" for OperatorAuditLog rows (transfer
deletes, batch creates/updates, daily-report locks/unlocks)
or "transfer" for TransferAudit rows (transfer creates / edits
/ status changes). The legacy Jinja page didn't expose this
field but it's useful for the SPA's row-key generation.
AdminAuditRow.title: AdminAuditRow

AdminAuditUserOption.description:
An entry in the user filter dropdown — every User on the
store sorted by full_name (then username).
AdminAuditUserOption.title: AdminAuditUserOption

AdminUserDetailResponse.description: Single-user fetch payload for the Edit form prefill.
AdminUserDetailResponse.title: AdminUserDetailResponse

AdminUserUpdateRequest.description:
PATCH-style update — fields omitted are left alone.

`password` is treated as "blank → keep current hash" by the
Service, mirroring the legacy form. Required-min-length on
the field would force every Edit submit to include a
password, breaking the existing UX, so we accept an empty
string and let the Service skip it.
AdminUserUpdateRequest.title: AdminUserUpdateRequest

AggregatedTotals.description: Sums across every row, returned alongside the rows.
AggregatedTotals.title: AggregatedTotals

AnnouncementCreateRequest.description:
POST body for /announcements. Mirrors the legacy
/superadmin/announcements/new form fields. `expires_days=0` (or
omitted) means no expiry — the banner stays up until the
superadmin disables it. `broadcast=True` queues the message for
the broadcast-email fan-out (only on create, never on edit).

`start_at_iso` is the optional ISO-8601 datetime (UTC) when the
banner should become visible — omit / empty means "start now".
Honored by `Announcement.visibility.active_announcements`, which
already skips not-yet-started rows.

start_at_iso.description: ISO-8601 UTC datetime when the banner should go live. Empty = start immediately.
start_at_iso.title: Start At Iso

AnnouncementCreateRequest.title: AnnouncementCreateRequest

AnnouncementRow.description:
One Announcement row. `is_visible` is a derived flag — True
when the row is_active AND inside its starts_at/expires_at window
— so the SPA doesn't have to recompute the date math client-side.
AnnouncementRow.title: AnnouncementRow

AnnouncementToggleRequest.description:
POST body for /announcements/{id}/toggle. Explicit
`is_active` so callers don't accidentally flip the wrong way
when the cached row is stale.
AnnouncementToggleRequest.title: AnnouncementToggleRequest

BankAccountListResponse.description:
Envelope for /bank/accounts. Order matches the Repository:
nickname → display_name → institution_name (case-insensitive)
+ id tie-break for stable rendering.
BankAccountListResponse.title: BankAccountListResponse

BankAccountRow.description:
One connected bank account. Fields mirror what the
/bank/transactions sidebar + the /bank/connect page render.
BankAccountRow.title: BankAccountRow

BankRuleListResponse.description:
Envelope for the /bank/rules read endpoint. Order matches the
Repository: priority asc, id asc tie-break — the same order the
auto-categorize sync walks them in, so what the UI shows is the
actual evaluation order.
BankRuleListResponse.title: BankRuleListResponse

BankRuleRow.description:
One operator-managed BankRule. Same fields the
/bank/rules HTML page exposes; the React rules-manager UI will
consume the same shape.
BankRuleRow.title: BankRuleRow

BankRuleToggleRequest.description:
POST body for /bank/rules/{id}/toggle. Explicit `enabled`
so callers don't accidentally flip the wrong way when their
cached row is stale.
BankRuleToggleRequest.title: BankRuleToggleRequest

BankRuleWriteRequest.description:
POST/PUT body for bank rule CRUD. Mirrors the legacy
/bank/rules/new + /bank/rules/<id>/edit forms.

`desc_match_type` must be "" (skip the description filter
entirely) or one of `contains`/`starts_with`/`equals`/`regex`.
Similarly `sign_filter` is "" / `credit` / `debit`.
`amount_min_cents` / `amount_max_cents` are absolute cents
(positive integers); None on either side means unbounded.
`target_kind` is required — what category the matching txn
gets tagged with.
BankRuleWriteRequest.title: BankRuleWriteRequest

BankTransactionListResponse.description:
Paginated response envelope. Mirrors the partial-render JSON
shape the legacy /bank/transactions page already returns.
BankTransactionListResponse.title: BankTransactionListResponse

BankTransactionRow.description:
One row in the /bank/transactions list. Wire shape mirrors
what the legacy template renders — id, date, label, amount in
dollars, category, etc.
BankTransactionRow.title: BankTransactionRow

BatchLinkedTransferRow.description:
Subset of Transfer columns the SPA's batch-detail page
renders. Kept narrower than the full TransferRow because
cross-module Pydantic re-export gets messy and the SPA
doesn't need every field here.
BatchLinkedTransferRow.title: BatchLinkedTransferRow

BatchResponse.description:
Single-batch payload used by the create / edit / detail
endpoints. Same shape as a row from the list endpoint.
BatchResponse.title: BatchResponse

BatchRow.description:
One ACH batch row. Mirrors the columns the legacy
`/batches` table renders + the computed totals
(transfers_total, variance, transfer_count) the SPA needs
to colour the variance cell.
BatchRow.title: BatchRow

BatchTransfersResponse.description:
Transfers linked to one ACH batch by `batch_id ==
batch_ref`. Same TransferRow shape the Transfers module
uses, mirrored here so the Batches read-side stays
self-contained.
BatchTransfersResponse.title: BatchTransfersResponse

BatchWriteRequest.description:
POST/PUT body for /batches. Mirrors the legacy form's
fields. Server pads `transfer_count` / `variance` /
`transfers_total` from the live Transfer table after the
write.
BatchWriteRequest.title: BatchWriteRequest

BillingPortalResponse.description:
Mint succeeded — `url` is the Stripe-hosted Billing Portal
URL the SPA should redirect the user to.
BillingPortalResponse.title: BillingPortalResponse

CategorizeRequest.description:
POST body for /bank/transactions/{txn_id}/categorize.

`target_kind` is a slug from `BANK_CATEGORIES_NON_POSTING` or
`_LINE_ITEM_KINDS` (e.g. "bank_charge_210", "cash_deposit").
`post_to_daily=False` keeps the assignment metadata-only and
skips creating the matching DailyLineItem (used when the
operator wants the P&L tag without a daily-book mirror).
CategorizeRequest.title: CategorizeRequest

CategorizeResponse.description:
Returned from categorize / uncategorize. Echoes the row's
new category state so the SPA can update without re-fetching.
CategorizeResponse.title: CategorizeResponse

ChangePasswordRequest.description:
POST body for /auth/change-password. Takes the user's
current password (proof of identity) plus the new password
twice. Same validation rules as the legacy /account/security
form — length ≥ 8 and the two new entries must match.
ChangePasswordRequest.title: ChangePasswordRequest

CheckoutSessionRequest.description:
POST body for /api/v2/billing/checkout. `plan` is one of the
keys recognised by `create_checkout_session` —
`basic` / `basic_yearly` / `pro` / `pro_yearly` (yearly options
only available when their Stripe price IDs are configured).
CheckoutSessionRequest.title: CheckoutSessionRequest

CheckoutSessionResponse.description:
Mint succeeded — `url` is the Stripe-hosted Checkout URL the
SPA should redirect the user to.
CheckoutSessionResponse.title: CheckoutSessionResponse

CreateTransferRequest.description:
POST body for /transfers. Mirrors the legacy `new_transfer`
Flask form fields. `federal_tax` is intentionally absent — the
server always recomputes from `(send_amount, service_type,
country, store)` so the client can't lie about the tax rate.
CreateTransferRequest.title: CreateTransferRequest

CustomerResponse.description:
Single-customer payload returned by GET /customers/{id}. Same
`customer` field name as CustomerUpsertResponse so the React
frontend can reuse the same parser.
CustomerResponse.title: CustomerResponse

CustomerSearchResponse.description:
Autocomplete response envelope.

`matches`: ILIKE substring hits on `full_name` or `phone_number`,
sorted by `updated_at` desc.
`suggestions`: fuzzy near-misses (different list so the UI can
label "Did you mean…?"). Empty unless the query is >= 4 chars
AND `matches` has room (< 5 entries).
CustomerSearchResponse.title: CustomerSearchResponse

CustomerUpsertRequest.description:
Body for POST upsert (the new transfer form's hidden submission).

All fields except `full_name` are optional — empty strings are
legal placeholders for senders without a phone or address on file.
`customer_id` is honored only when the target lives in the
caller's owner umbrella (enforced by the Repository layer).
CustomerUpsertRequest.title: CustomerUpsertRequest

CustomerUpsertResponse.description:
Single-customer payload returned by upsert. Same shape as one
`CustomerRow` so the frontend can reuse the row component.
CustomerUpsertResponse.title: CustomerUpsertResponse

DailyReportResponse.description:
Wrapped single-report response. None when the store hasn't
logged a report on that date — clients distinguish via 404 at
the Controller layer.
DailyReportResponse.title: DailyReportResponse

DailyReportRow.description:
One day's roll-up. Pre-computes receipts / disbursements /
net so the React table doesn't have to.

Carries the full DailyReport field set — the editor hydrates
every input from this payload, line-item-derived fields display
as read-only "Auto" tiles, and the real-time totals strip sums
them client-side as the cashier types.
DailyReportRow.title: DailyReportRow

DailyReportUpdateRequest.description:
PUT body for /daily/{store_id}/{date}. Only the editable
top-level totals + notes — line-item-derived fields
(cash_purchases, drops, etc.) come from their own tables and
aren't writable here. Every numeric field is optional so the
SPA can submit a partial form (only what the cashier edited).
DailyReportUpdateRequest.title: DailyReportUpdateRequest

DiscountCodeRow.description:
One DiscountCode row. `value_label` carries the legacy
derived display text ("$5 off" / "20% off") so the SPA renders
without recomputing. `is_redeemable` is True when the code is
active AND not expired AND under any max_redemptions cap.
DiscountCodeRow.title: DiscountCodeRow

DiscountCodeToggleRequest.description:
POST body for /superadmin/discounts/{id}/toggle. Explicit
`is_active` so callers don't accidentally flip the wrong way
when their cached row is stale.
DiscountCodeToggleRequest.title: DiscountCodeToggleRequest

FeatureFlagCreateRequest.description:
POST body for /feature-flags. Mirrors the legacy
/superadmin/features/new form. `key` is slug-style — lowercase
letters, digits, underscores; the convention is `addon_<thing>`
for paid add-ons or `<feature>` for general toggles.
FeatureFlagCreateRequest.title: FeatureFlagCreateRequest

FeatureFlagToggleRequest.description:
POST body for /feature-flags/{key}/toggle. Explicit
`enabled_by_default` so callers don't accidentally flip the
wrong way on stale data.
FeatureFlagToggleRequest.title: FeatureFlagToggleRequest

ForgotPasswordRequest.description:
POST body for /auth/forgot-password. Always responds 200
regardless of whether the email exists — the legacy contract
is "Check your email" so attackers can't enumerate registered
addresses.
ForgotPasswordRequest.title: ForgotPasswordRequest

LineItemCreateRequest.description:
POST body for /daily/{store}/{date}/line-items. Validates
against the same parsers the legacy form uses (`parse_at_time`,
`parse_amount`) so error messages match for cutover parity.
LineItemCreateRequest.title: LineItemCreateRequest

LineItemListResponse.description:
Wrapped list. Optional kind filter narrows the result;
omit to return every kind for the day.
LineItemListResponse.title: LineItemListResponse

LineItemRow.description:
One DailyLineItem (drop, check deposit, cash expense,
return payback, etc.) on a daily report. The line-item
family is discriminated by `kind`; see LINE_ITEM_KINDS.
LineItemRow.title: LineItemRow

LoginCrossStoreRequest.description:
POST body for /auth/login-cross-store. The SPA's generic
landing page doesn't know which store a user belongs to — this
endpoint takes username + password only and looks up the
user's home store across all stores (first match wins, like
the legacy Flask `/login` POST). Employees get rejected here
because they're expected to use their store's slug-scoped
sign-in URL.
LoginCrossStoreRequest.title: LoginCrossStoreRequest

LoginRequest.description:
POST body for /auth/login. `store_id` is None for the
superadmin scope; positive integer otherwise.
LoginRequest.title: LoginRequest

LoginResponse.description:
Login response. Two shapes:

- **Full success**: `access_token` is the bearer JWT the client
  must send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on subsequent
  calls. `requires_totp` is False, `pending_token` is None.

- **2FA pending**: `requires_totp=True` and `pending_token` is a
  short-lived JWT (5min) the SPA exchanges via
  `/auth/login/totp` or `/auth/login/recovery` for a real
  `access_token`. In this shape `access_token` is empty.

Clients should branch on `requires_totp` first.
LoginResponse.title: LoginResponse

MTBreakdownResponse.description:
Per-company MT breakdown for a single (store, date). Empty
`rows` means the store has no MT companies configured (a fresh
install before the company list is populated).
MTBreakdownResponse.title: MTBreakdownResponse

MTBreakdownRowResponse.description:
One company's row in the MT breakdown read response.

Carries BOTH `saved_*` (operator-edited persisted values) and
`auto_*` (transfer-log aggregate). The React editor pre-fills
each input from saved when present, falls back to auto on a
fresh day, and renders a "reset to auto" affordance when the
two diverge.
MTBreakdownRowResponse.title: MTBreakdownRowResponse

MTBreakdownWriteRequest.description:
Bulk-replace payload for the per-company MT breakdown. Every
row in `rows` becomes a `MoneyTransferSummary` insert (or no
insert at all when every field is zero), and the daily
report's `money_transfer` field is updated to the new grand
total in one transaction.
MTBreakdownWriteRequest.title: MTBreakdownWriteRequest

MTBreakdownWriteRow.description:
Operator-edited per-company values. Sent as a list inside
MTBreakdownWriteRequest.
MTBreakdownWriteRow.title: MTBreakdownWriteRow

MonthLogged.description: One (year, month) entry the store has logged.
MonthLogged.title: MonthLogged

MonthlyResponse.description:
Wrapped single-month payload. `report` is None when no
row exists for the (year, month) — clients distinguish via
a 404 at the controller layer.
MonthlyResponse.title: MonthlyResponse

MonthlyRow.description:
One MonthlyFinancial row — the per-store, per-month P&L
breakdown. Keep field names matching the model + legacy
template so the SPA's table can be a generic key→value loop.
MonthlyRow.title: MonthlyRow

MonthlyUpdateRequest.description:
PUT body for /monthly/{year}/{month}.

All numeric fields optional — the SPA can submit only what
the operator edited. Auto-derived fields (cash_purchases,
cash_expenses, return_check_gl, bank_charges_total when
bank-sync data exists, etc.) are NOT in this schema; the
server overwrites them from the daily ledger / bank
transactions / return-check workflow regardless of what the
client sends.
MonthlyUpdateRequest.title: MonthlyUpdateRequest

MonthsLoggedResponse.description:
Wrapped list of all (year, month) pairs with rows.
Sorted newest-first so the SPA can default to the most
recent.
MonthsLoggedResponse.title: MonthsLoggedResponse

NotificationsResponse.description:
Per-user notification preferences. `trial_toggle_applies`
tells the SPA whether to render the Trial-ending toggle as
interactive (True) or grey/informational (False — already
paid, or role doesn't own a trial).
NotificationsResponse.title: NotificationsResponse

NotificationsUpdateRequest.description:
PUT body. Both fields optional — None = don't touch.
Empty payload is a no-op (HTTP 200 with current state).
NotificationsUpdateRequest.title: NotificationsUpdateRequest

OwnerConnectCodeRow.description:
One owner-generated connect code (the 8-char invite a store
admin redeems on /admin/settings to link their store).
OwnerConnectCodeRow.title: OwnerConnectCodeRow

OwnerLocationsResponse.description:
Per-store rows for /api/v2/owner/locations.

`total` is the unfiltered umbrella size (so the SPA can
distinguish "owner has no stores connected yet" from "search
returned zero matches").
OwnerLocationsResponse.title: OwnerLocationsResponse

OwnerPLRollupResponse.description:
Side-by-side monthly P&L for every store in the owner umbrella.
Sorted by net income desc — strongest performers first. `year` /
`month` echo back so the SPA's pager knows what to navigate from.
`year_choices` is the set of years with at least one P&L row across
the umbrella, used to render a year-dropdown without an extra
request.
OwnerPLRollupResponse.title: OwnerPLRollupResponse

OwnerPLRollupRow.description:
One store's monthly P&L row for /owner/pl-rollup. `has_pl` is
False when there's no MonthlyFinancial row for the (store, year,
month) yet — UI can render a "—" placeholder instead of $0.00.
OwnerPLRollupRow.title: OwnerPLRollupRow

OwnerSignupRequest.description:
POST body for /auth/signup/owner. Mirrors the legacy
/signup/owner Jinja form. Returns a JWT on success so the SPA
drops the new owner straight onto /owner/dashboard.
OwnerSignupRequest.title: OwnerSignupRequest

OwnerSignupResponse.description:
Same shape as LoginResponse — the SPA reuses the standard
auth handoff (set token, then navigate). `store_id` is always
None for owners (they manage many stores via invite codes).
OwnerSignupResponse.title: OwnerSignupResponse

OwnerStoreRow.description:
One store in the owner's umbrella, decorated with period-scoped
operational stats (transfers / volume / over-short) and the
company mix that drove that volume.
OwnerStoreRow.title: OwnerStoreRow

OwnerUnlinkRequest.description:
POST body for /owner/unlink/{store_id}. Empty schema today
(the store_id is in the path), but `extra="forbid"` keeps it
explicit + future-extensible.
OwnerUnlinkRequest.title: OwnerUnlinkRequest

PeriodSummaryResponse.description:
Date-range payload. `rows` are per-day; summary fields are
sums across them.
PeriodSummaryResponse.title: PeriodSummaryResponse

ProfileResponse.description:
Full payload for the /app/account/profile page on first
paint. Includes editable fields, read-only metadata, and the
canonical timezone list so the SPA doesn't have to ship its
own copy.
ProfileResponse.title: ProfileResponse

ProfileUpdateRequest.description:
PUT body. All four editable fields are individually
optional — the SPA could submit only the dirty ones — but
the legacy form always sends all four, so the service layer
treats absent == 'don't change'.

Validation lives in the Service so the legacy app._update_user_profile
helper and the FastAPI path can share rules.
ProfileUpdateRequest.title: ProfileUpdateRequest

RecoveryLoginRequest.description:
POST body for /auth/login/recovery. Exchange the 2FA-pending
token + a single-use recovery code for a real access token.
The recovery code is consumed on success.
RecoveryLoginRequest.title: RecoveryLoginRequest

ReferralCodeResponse.description:
Self-service referral page payload. `share_url` is the full
/signup?ref=<code> URL on the canonical host (built server-side
so the SPA doesn't have to know the host).
ReferralCodeResponse.title: ReferralCodeResponse

ReferralPreviewResponse.description:
GET /auth/referral/{code} return shape. Powers the green
'You'll get $X off' banner that shows up on /signup when the
code resolves to an active ReferralCode row.
ReferralPreviewResponse.title: ReferralPreviewResponse

ReferralRedemptionRow.description: One redemption row in the History table on the referrals page.
ReferralRedemptionRow.title: ReferralRedemptionRow

ReportCategory.description:
Group of related reports (Sales / Financial / Operations /
Customers / Audit). The icon is an inline stroke SVG matching
the rest of the design-system iconography (CLAUDE.md).
ReportCategory.title: ReportCategory

ReportRow.description:
One report card on the categorized index. `url` is the
Flask drilldown path (legacy templates still own per-report
rendering for now); `status` is `ready` or `coming_soon`.
ReportRow.title: ReportRow

ResetPasswordRequest.description:
POST body for /auth/reset-password. Uses the raw
one-time token from the emailed reset link.
ResetPasswordRequest.title: ResetPasswordRequest

ReturnCheckPaymentResponse.description:
Single-row payload returned by POST/DELETE payment endpoints.
Includes the refreshed parent ``return_check`` so the client
can update the recovered_total + status pill in one round-trip.
ReturnCheckPaymentResponse.title: ReturnCheckPaymentResponse

ReturnCheckPaymentWriteRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /return-checks/{id}/payments``.

``paid_on`` is the YYYY-MM-DD the cashier received the
installment; the matching ``DailyLineItem`` auto-creates with
this report_date. ``method`` is free-text but the SPA's form
constrains it to ``cash / check / zelle / wire / money_order /
other`` for consistency.
ReturnCheckPaymentWriteRequest.title: ReturnCheckPaymentWriteRequest

ReturnCheckRow.description:
One bounced-check row. Mirrors the columns the legacy
/return-checks list page renders.
ReturnCheckRow.title: ReturnCheckRow

ReturnCheckWriteRequest.description:
POST/PUT body. Status transitions go through dedicated
endpoints, not via this schema.
ReturnCheckWriteRequest.title: ReturnCheckWriteRequest

RosterResponse.description:
Wrapped roster. Same shape pattern as the rest of the
Transfers module's read-side payloads.
RosterResponse.title: RosterResponse

SignupRequest.description:
POST body for /auth/signup. Mirrors the legacy /signup
Jinja form. Returns a JWT on success so the SPA can drop
the new admin straight onto the dashboard without a second
login round-trip.
SignupRequest.title: SignupRequest

SignupResponse.description:
Same shape as LoginResponse — the SPA uses identical code
paths to handle both flows.
SignupResponse.title: SignupResponse

StoreInfoRow.description:
Read shape — fields the SPA's settings page renders.
Slug / plan / billing fields are read-only here; the
superadmin owns those.
StoreInfoRow.title: StoreInfoRow

StoreInfoUpdateRequest.description:
PUT body. Only the operator-editable fields. Slug,
plan, billing, retention etc. stay server-managed.
StoreInfoUpdateRequest.title: StoreInfoUpdateRequest

StoreLookupResponse.description:
GET /auth/store-by-slug/{slug} — public lookup so the SPA's
per-store login page can render the store name in its branding
pane before the user authenticates. Inactive / unknown slugs
return 404.
StoreLookupResponse.title: StoreLookupResponse

StoreOverrideRequest.description:
PUT body for /feature-flags/{key}/stores/{store_id}.
Sets (or replaces) a per-store override. To clear it back to
the global default, DELETE the same path.
StoreOverrideRequest.title: StoreOverrideRequest

SuperadminAnomalyRow.description:
One platform anomaly row. `kind` is one of
`quiet_store` / `big_over_short`; `severity` is
`low` / `medium` / `high`. `description` is the human-readable
explanation the SPA renders verbatim. `href` is the legacy
drill-down URL — once those pages migrate it'll point to
/app/* equivalents.
SuperadminAnomalyRow.title: SuperadminAnomalyRow

SuperadminAuditRow.description:
One row from the platform-wide superadmin_audit_log. Snapshot
fields (admin_name, action, target_type, target_id, details,
created_at) — enough to render the table without a JOIN.
SuperadminAuditRow.title: SuperadminAuditRow

SuperadminReportCategory.description:
Group of related reports — Platform Health / Revenue /
Stripe / Trial Funnel / Feature Adoption / Support. The
`icon` is an inline stroke SVG matching the rest of the
sidebar/nav iconography (CLAUDE.md design system).
SuperadminReportCategory.title: SuperadminReportCategory

SuperadminReportRow.description:
One report card on the report-center index. `url` is the
Flask drilldown path (still on Flask until each report
individually migrates); `status` is `ready` when an endpoint
backs the report or `coming_soon` when only a placeholder is
declared. The SPA renders the `View` button on `ready` rows
and a disabled `Coming soon` pill on the rest.
SuperadminReportRow.title: SuperadminReportRow

SuperadminStoreCreateRequest.description:
POST body for /superadmin/stores.

Identity fields mirror the Jinja form's required set: `name` and
`slug` are mandatory; the rest default to empty strings (matches
the legacy ``request.form.get("phone","")`` style). `plan`
accepts any of the four canonical values though the legacy form
only ever submitted trial / basic / pro.

The initial admin user is also created in the same transaction.
Defaults match the legacy handler so an operator can submit just
name + slug + admin_password and get a usable store back —
`admin_username` falls back to "admin", `admin_name` to "Store
Admin", and `admin_password` is required (the legacy fallback to
"changeme123!" was a footgun and is dropped here).
SuperadminStoreCreateRequest.title: SuperadminStoreCreateRequest

SuperadminStoreDetailRow.description:
Full store payload for the edit form prefill.

Superset of `SuperadminStoreRow` (the list-view row): adds
address + federal_tax_rate which the form needs but the table
doesn't render.
SuperadminStoreDetailRow.title: SuperadminStoreDetailRow

SuperadminStoreRow.description:
One store on the platform-wide stores list. Fields chosen to
cover the legacy `/superadmin/stores` table view: identity,
plan, trial state, retention timer, and Stripe linkage.
SuperadminStoreRow.title: SuperadminStoreRow

SuperadminStoreUpdateRequest.description:
PATCH body for /superadmin/stores/{id}.

Every field is optional — clients pass only what they want to
change. Slug uniqueness is enforced at the route level (a
duplicate returns 409 with `field=slug`).

`plan` is included because the legacy form drops the operator
on a /new page that lets them pick the plan before save; the
edit page needs the same affordance so a comped store can be
moved between plans without going through Stripe.
SuperadminStoreUpdateRequest.title: SuperadminStoreUpdateRequest

TVDisplayBankRow.description:
One bank within a country, with its filled-in rate cells.
`rates` is a sparse map keyed by mt_company; absent entries are
rendered as "—" on the public board.
TVDisplayBankRow.title: TVDisplayBankRow

TVDisplayClaimRequest.description:
The 6-char code the operator typed in from a Fire TV showing
the pairing screen. Server normalises (strips non-alnum, uppercases)
before lookup; client may send it raw.
TVDisplayClaimRequest.title: TVDisplayClaimRequest

TVDisplayCountryCreateRequest.description:
Add a new country section. Country picker on the landing page
submits the ISO-2 plus the human-readable name; mt_companies is
optional (can be filled in later from the country editor).
TVDisplayCountryCreateRequest.title: TVDisplayCountryCreateRequest

TVDisplayCountryCreateResponse.description:
The new country row — caller redirects into the editor for
that country_id to fill in banks + rates.
TVDisplayCountryCreateResponse.title: TVDisplayCountryCreateResponse

TVDisplayCountryDetailResponse.description:
Full drill-down for one country: header config + bank matrix.
`mt_companies` is the column-header list (already split for the
SPA), preserving order; `banks` carries one TVDisplayBankRow per
payout bank, each with their filled-in rate cells.
TVDisplayCountryDetailResponse.title: TVDisplayCountryDetailResponse

TVDisplayCountryStat.description:
One country section as it appears on the admin landing.
`mt_companies` is the CSV column header list — stays a single
string so the SPA can preserve column order without normalizing.
TVDisplayCountryStat.title: TVDisplayCountryStat

TVDisplayOverviewResponse.description:
Everything the SPA admin landing needs in one envelope.
`public_url` is the absolute /tv/<token> URL the operator hands
to a tablet/Chromecast; the SPA renders it as a copy-to-clipboard
target. `active_pairing` is None when no Fire TV is paired.
TVDisplayOverviewResponse.title: TVDisplayOverviewResponse

TVDisplayRegenerateTokenResponse.description:
Result of rotating the public_token. The SPA refreshes its
overview state from this, since the URL the operator has to hand
out changed.

post.description:

up across every store. Employees are rejected here so they
use their store's slug-scoped sign-in page (parity with the
legacy Flask `/login` POST).

for a real access token. Recovery code is consumed on success.

Exchange a 2FA-pending token + 6-digit TOTP code for a real
access token. Pending token comes from the previous
`/auth/login` (or `/auth/login-cross-store`) response when
`requires_totp=True`.

User has saved their recovery codes. Exchange the still-valid
pending token for a real access token. Symmetric with
/login/totp and /login/recovery — same envelope shape.

Verify the user's first 6-digit code, mark enrollment
complete, and return one-shot recovery codes. The SPA holds

QR SVG + secret + chunks the SPA renders. Idempotent — refreshes
return the same secret so a half-scanned QR stays valid.

Clear both the access-token + refresh-token cookies and
revoke the refresh row server-side.

The access JWT is still cryptographically valid until its
30-minute exp, but the browser no longer ships either cookie
and the refresh row's ``revoked_at`` is set — so even an
attacker who captured the access cookie before logout can
only use it for the remaining minutes of its TTL, and the
matching refresh chain is already burned.

post.description:
Rotate the refresh token + mint a fresh access JWT.

The SPA's ``api()`` helper hits this when a regular API call
401s — silent recovery from an expired access cookie.
Successful refresh sets new ``db_access_token`` + new
``db_refresh_token`` cookies (rotation: the old refresh row
is revoked and chained to the new one via ``rotated_to_id``).

Failures clear both cookies and return 401:
  * No refresh cookie → not logged in
  * Unknown jti → forged or row-deleted (rare)
  * Already revoked → replay (legitimate user rotated past it)
  * Expired → past the 14-day TTL

post.description:

— if the admin User insert fails the Store row rolls back.

Slug normalization (lowercase + dashes) matches the legacy
handler. Duplicate slugs return 409 with `field=slug` so the SPA
can render the field-level error inline.

get.description:

every field the edit form binds against (identity + plan +

patch.description:

Every field is optional — only the keys present in the body get
applied. Slug uniqueness is re-validated on rename (a duplicate
returns 409 with `field=slug`). The audit row's `details` lists
the keys that changed so the audit log shows what was touched
even when the values are sensitive (email).

  - Trial extension → POST /superadmin/stores/{id}/extend-trial
  - Toggle active   → POST /superadmin/stores/{id}/toggle-active
  - Comp plan       → POST /superadmin/stores/{id}/comp-plan
  - Add-on toggle   → POST /superadmin/stores/{id}/addons/...
Those flows ship separately because they have their own audit
actions + side effects (cancel-related state cleanup, retention
timer reset, etc.).
